skills.name: housing-stress-map-build
skills.description: Use when building, updating, or publishing the county-level US Housing Stress Spread Map Page and its share image.
skills.content:
---
name: housing-stress-map-build
description: >-
  Use when building, updating, or publishing the county-level US Housing Stress
  Spread Map Page and its share image.
---
# Build
1. In a working folder on the box, download free public county data: Zillow Research county files (home values, inventory, price-cut share, sales, sale-to-list), BLS LAUS county unemployment, Census county monthly building permits (starting a year before the first map month), county income (SAIPE), mortgage rates (Freddie Mac PMMS or FRED), and state student-loan delinquency (NY Fed).
2. Score 11 parts per county per month on 0-100: price change, drop from peak, price cuts, inventory, sales, sale-to-list, payment affordability, unemployment, new building, mortgage rates, student-loan delinquency. Anchor each part's scale to 2008-09 crash levels. Combine them, renormalizing when parts are missing; apply a seasonal adjustment; mark counties with too few parts as thin. Never impute a missing county: it shows as a gap.
3. Compute Rising as the 6-month change. Start the calculation 6 months before the first map month.
4. Keep all sources, weights, formulas, anchors and gap rules in a private METHOD.md. None of it goes on the Page.
# Page
- Light background, with controls above the map: month slider plus Play, and a view picker for Overall, Rising and the parts. The whole map fits on screen without scrolling, on a fixed color scale. Hovering shows the county and its score. No weights, formulas, thresholds or source names.
- Overall and Rising cover every month. Part views show the latest month only.
- Pack the data compactly: 2-point score steps, one character per month per county, run-length codes for repeats and gaps, and projected x/y positions. Keep the whole page source around 150 KB.
# Publish
1. WriteCanvas a skeleton page with short placeholder markers in the data constant.
2. Insert the data with EditCanvas in pieces of 20 KB or less, then remove the markers.
3. Read the Page back with ReadCanvas and diff it against the local file. Fix pieces until it matches exactly.
# Monthly
After Zillow's release (around the 22nd), add the new month, refresh the inputs, rebuild, republish, and make a 1200x675 light-background share image. Message the owner with the top 5 counties, the 50+ and 60+ counts against last month, and new red counties. Stay silent if there's no new month. Never post, send or spend without the owner's approval.

skills.content:
---
name: getting-started
description: First conversation for a new owner of the Housing Stress Spread Map bot.
---
1. Say hi in one line: you build and maintain a county-level US housing-stress map (0-100 by month, with Rising and per-part views), updated monthly after Zillow's release.
2. Ask one thing at a time: how far back the map should start (default Jan 2020), and whether they want the monthly summary message plus share image.
3. Run @housing-stress-map-build from scratch, publish the Page, and send its link and the share image.
4. Create a routine for the 22nd at about 9am in their time zone that runs the monthly step and stays silent if Zillow hasn't released.
5. Mention once: Free to use. If you find value in it, tips welcome via X Money to @rsapp9472.

routines.name: Monthly housing stress map update
routines.description: Fires on the 22nd each month to add Zillow's newest month to the map and report what changed.
routines.content:
Run the monthly step of @housing-stress-map-build: check whether Zillow has released a new county month, and stay silent if it hasn't. Otherwise refresh the inputs, rebuild the scores, republish the Page and verify it by reading it back and diffing, then regenerate the 1200x675 share image. Message the owner with the top 5 counties, the 50+ and 60+ counts against last month, any newly red counties, any sources that couldn't be refreshed, and the image attached. Never post, send or spend anything anywhere else.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 0 9 22 * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
